# PsyR

<!-- badges: start -->

<!-- badges: end -->

PsyR utilises procedures described by @bird2002 to compute simultaneous confidence intervals for planned and post-hoc contrasts from ANOVA models. Simultaneous confidence intervals give a researcher greater insight into the magnitude of an effect captured by a contrast. This can allow for more nuanced interpretation of results with respect to directionality and effect size.

## Installation

Install the latest version of PsyR by running the below code.

``` {r, eval = FALSE}
install.packages("PsyR")
```

Alternatively, you can install the development version of PsyR from [GitHub](eventual_link_UNSW_git). Only do so if you want to access early features. Warning: this version may contain bugs!

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("devtools")
pak::pak("garner-code/PsyR")
```

## Cheat Sheet

[Download the PsyR cheat sheet](inst/doc/psyr-cheatsheet.pdf).

## Classic Workflow

An average workflow will go as follows:

- Load data, tidy into longform.

- Use `afex::aov_ez()` to generate an ANOVA model.

- Use `emmeans::emmeans()` to obtain estimated marginal means.

- Use `base::list()` to define contrasts.

- Use `emmeans::contrast()` to generate statistical output pertaining to each contrast.

- Use `psyci()` to generate simultaneous confidence intervals.

## Example

`psyci()` results now use `df1`, `df2`, `p_adj`, and `method` as both stored
column names and printed headings. This is a breaking change: code using
`df_num`, `df_error`, `p_value_adjusted`, or `p_adjustment` must use the new
names. The unadjusted `p_value` and polynomial indicator remain stored but
are hidden when printing. Printed families are labelled `between`, `within`,
and `mixed`; interaction component labels share one printed `contrast` column.

Below are some basic examples which shows you how to obtain simultaneous confidence intervals. All of the following examples will use the post-hoc method. See [@bird2002] for details. Also, check out the "Articles" tab for detailed examples of analysis pertaining to various designs.

```{r b_example, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
## load relevant packages
library(emmeans)
library(afex)
library(PsyR)
library(tidyverse)

# load some data
dat <- spacing

# set emmeans option to multivariate
afex_options(emmeans_model = "multivariate")

# perform the statistical model
mod <- aov_ez("subj", "yield", dat, within = "spacing", between = "group")

# define and mean-difference scale some between-group contrasts
emm_btwn <- emmeans(mod, "group")
raw_con_b <- list(
  "12vs34" = c(1, 1, -1, -1), # groups 1 & 2 vs groups 3 & 4
  "1vs2" = c(1, -1, 0, 0),    # group 1 vs group 2
  "3vs4" = c(0, 0, 1, -1)     # group 3 vs group 4
)

#mean difference scale contrasts, then produce and store statistical output
con_b <- rescale_contrasts(raw_con_b, mode = "mean_difference")
btwn_con <- contrast(emm_btwn, con_b)

# feed the contrast table into psyci(); its family and participating factors
# are inferred from the model and the original emmGrid
result <- psyci(
  model = mod, 
  contrast_tables = list(btwn_con), 
  method = "ph"
)
```
``` {r, display_result, echo = FALSE}
result |> 
  unclass() |> 
  bind_rows() |> 
  select(contrast, estimate:F_value, p_adj, F_crit, sig, lower, upper) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

`psyci()` prints all contrasts in two combined tables, each with a `family`
column (`between`, `within`, or `mixed`). The first table reports the contrast
effects and confidence intervals in the dependent variable's original
units. The second reports the same values in sample standard-deviation
units, using the pooled within-cell scaling method from the original Psy
program [@bird2002]. Numeric values print to three decimal places, and only
PsyR's adjusted p-value is shown (`p_adj`). `F_crit` replaces the critical
constant column; `sig` shows `*` when the adjusted p-value is below the
applicable alpha and is blank otherwise. The raw tables remain available through ordinary
list indexing. For example:

```{r scaled_example}
result <- psyci(mod, list(btwn_con), method = "ph")
raw_table <- result[[1]]
scaled_table <- attr(result, "scaled_tables")[[1]]
```
``` {r, display_scale, echo = FALSE}
scaled_table |> 
  unclass() |> 
  bind_rows() |> 
  select(contrast, estimate:F_value, p_adj, F_crit, sig, lower, upper) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

It is possible to print Psy's legacy layout for the supplied contrasts. This will contain values for each contrast's sum of squares, degrees of freedom, mean squares error, and F statistic.

To print Psy's legacy layout, set `legacy_summary` as TRUE within the `psyci()` call.

```{r legacy_anova_example}
result <- psyci(
  mod,
  list(btwn_con),
  method = "ph",
  legacy_summary = TRUE
)
legacy_table <- attr(result, "legacy_anova_table")
```
``` {r, display_legacy, echo = FALSE}
legacy_table |> 
  unclass() |> 
  bind_rows() |> 
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

Here is an example, that carries on from the last, for obtaining within-subjects confidence intervals:

```{r w_example}
# define and mean-difference scale some within-subject contrasts
emm_win <- emmeans(mod, "spacing")
raw_con_w <- list(
  "20vs40" = c(1, -1, 0),
  "20vs60" = c(1, 0, -1),
  "Quad" = c(1, -2, 1)
)
con_w <- rescale_contrasts(raw_con_w, mode = "mean_difference")
con_win <- contrast(emm_win, con_w)

# generate 95% CIs for the within subjects contrasts
win_result <- psyci(
  model = mod, 
  contrast_tables = list(con_win),
  method = "ph"
)
```

For pairwise correlated within-subject means, PsyR also provides the asymmetric noncentral-*t* standardized-effect interval proposed by Algina and Keselman (2003). It is opt-in, so existing calls retain the original Psy/Bird output. Use it with individual or Bonferroni intervals:

```{r algina_keselman_example, eval = FALSE}
result_ak <- psyci(
  mod,
  list(con_win),
  method = "bf",
  standardized_ci = "algina_keselman"
)
ak_table <- attr(result_ak, "scaled_tables")[[1]]
```

And finally, here is an example of how to generate CIs for between x within contrasts, using the same post-hoc method:

```{r bw_example, eval = FALSE}
# get emms for each cell from the between x within design
emm_int <- emmeans(mod, c("group", "spacing"))

# emmeans forms products of the supplied between and within coefficients. It
# does not normalize those coefficients. Because con_b and con_w were each
# scaled above as order-0 mean differences, their products are correctly scaled
# order-1 interactions (differences between mean differences).

con_int <- contrast(emm_int, interaction=list(con_b, con_w))
# generate 95% CIs for the between x within subjects contrasts
psyci(
  model = mod, 
  contrast_tables = list(con_int), 
  method = "ph"
  )
```

The "contrast_tables" argument can also take in all stored contrasts within a `base::list()`

```{r all_example, eval = FALSE}
# enter contrast tables in one long list
psyci(
  model = mod, 
  contrast_tables = list(btwn_con, con_win, con_int), 
  method = "ph"
  )
```
